chapter: Family and the lake excursion boats
title: Madisonville boats and shipyards
summary: Ernie names the boats that ran from Madisonville to New Orleans, then the Susquehanna, with bands every summer. He describes the Jahncke and Vowles shipyards and hand cars to the wharf.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Working the Streckfus riverboats with Fate Marable

blocks.x: And you said the musicians used to come over and play on the boat. You see, there's a camellia and the handover and the victor. That was the tree boats running from Madison to New Orleans. And after the camellia and the handover stopped running, they had the Susquehanna. And the bands used to run across the river lake every summer. And then they had
the Madisonville. The Susquehanna used to run the manover. And the Madisonville used to run the manover.

I got a postcard the other day that showed the wharf I think where the camellia landed. It looked like a railroad track running out there in the lake. Is there a train or street car? What ran out there? Do you know? That was Mandeville I think.

That was in Mandeville. No, wait a minute. No, wait a minute. No. In Madisonville. In Madisonville. In Madisonville. I'll tell you what they was. You see, they had two shipyards there. They had Janky shipyards and they had Vowles shipyards. And on Vowles shipyards they had a train track that would run directly to the end of the river. With those two bumpers on like they got through trains. And they used to have those small hand cars that you would pull it. And we used to ride them and go right up to the wharf with it. Like that.
